facts.text: Chippewa Falls takes its name from the Chippewa River, which itself is named after the Ojibwe people.
In 1972, computer pioneer Seymour Cray founded Cray Research in Chippewa Falls after running a lab there at Control Data Corporation.
Before roads, the Chippewa River’s watershed held more timber than the Wisconsin River, and the only way to move it out was down the river through Chippewa Falls.
The Chippewa Falls Public Library is digitizing its microfilmed newspapers in the Local History Room, keeping the town’s print legacy alive.
A self‑guided Historic Walking Tour lets visitors admire Chippewa Falls’ charming architecture, local shops, and farmers’ markets while strolling the town’s streets.
The original McDonell High School building, perched above downtown, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
